record.original_question: For the proposed infinite-chamber mechanical model of inverse cascade, is there an analogous mechanism in real hydrodynamics, and can the parameters n_i, m_i, and r_i be chosen so that the apparatus transfers energy to the first few chambers as intended?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following idealized mechanical model intended to mimic an inverse energy cascade. The apparatus consists of a countable sequence of chambers indexed by i = 1, 2, 3, …. The i-th chamber contains n_i identical rigid balls, each of mass m_i and radius r_i, which undergo elastic collisions among themselves and with the walls of the chamber. Neighbouring chambers are coupled so that collisions can transfer kinetic energy between balls in chamber i and balls in chamber i+1 (for instance via a shared wall or piston, with elastic interactions). Energy is injected into the system at small scales (large i) and one seeks to observe a net flow of energy toward large scales (small i), i.e. into the first few chambers.

(a) Is there an analogous mechanism in real (continuum) hydrodynamics — for example in two-dimensional incompressible fluid flow, where an inverse energy cascade is known to occur — which corresponds to this mechanical model?

(b) Can the parameters n_i, m_i, r_i (i ≥ 1) be chosen so that, starting from energy supplied to chambers with large index, the apparatus transfers a positive fraction of the total energy to the first few chambers (those with small i) in the long-time limit?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears as an open problem in a 2022/2023 collection of open problems in geometric hydrodynamics. No subsequent literature found that resolves the question of whether the parameters of such an infinite-chamber mechanical apparatus can be tuned to achieve an inverse energy cascade, nor identifying a precise hydrodynamic analogue. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: A collection of open problems including mechanical models of direct and inverse cascades.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an open problem in a survey of open problems in geometric hydrodynamics; no resolution has been published.
